svg.title: Canary Vision Doorbell: button, glow ring and speaker wiring
svg.desc: XIAO D1 reads the button through a 1k resistor with a 100nF filter; XIAO D2 drives a 2N3904 low-side switch for the button LED ring, powered from the XIAO 5V pin; XIAO D10 feeds a two-pole RC filter, a 1uF coupling cap and a 10k/2.2k divider into a PAM8302A amplifier that drives the speaker. The firmware holds D8 low. D0, D3 and D9 are never wired: on the stacked Grove Vision AI V2 they are the module SYNC output, its reset and its SPI MISO output.
svg.text: Canary Vision Doorbell — button, glow ring and speaker (XIAO ESP32-S3 / -C3 on the Grove Vision AI V2)
Every red 5V tag connects to the XIAO 5V pin. Every ⏚ symbol connects to the XIAO GND pin. Numbered circles 1–8 are the build order (list at the bottom).
Vision AI V2 stacked on top
nothing to wire: the module’s SPI clock, kept still
Lit button — back side · 6 V LED
flat side toward you, legs down
R8 + R9 drop the 3.3 V signal to about 0.6 V so the amp does not distort.
Build order — button and glow ring
XIAO D1 → C2 (100 nF) → GND. Solder C2 right at the XIAO.
XIAO D1 → R5 (1 kΩ) → button NO.
• Multimeter on continuity: 5V and GND must NOT beep. D1, D2 and D10 must only beep to the parts shown above.
• Never wire D0, D3 or D9: on the Vision AI V2 they are the module’s SYNC output, its RESET (silkscreen RST) and its SPI MISO output.
• Amp back-side names: Vin = 2-5VDC · SD = Shutdown · Gnd = Ground · A+ = Audio In+ · A− = Audio In− · + / − = 4-8R Load.
• Use the 6 V LED version of the button. A 3 V version needs a 100 Ω resistor in series with LED+.
